articleTitle: Intelligent Control of PMSM-Driven Electric Vehicles Using Fuzzy Logic and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Transport electrification is a trend research topic and one of the biggest nowadays challenges. This paper discusses intelligent hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) control using direct torque control (DTC) based genetic algorithm (GA). An optimized estimator is used to control the electric vehicle (EV) using direct torque control technique. A proposed cost function was used along with DTC-SVM based genetic algorithm to provide a self-tuning for the three used vehicle regulators. By taking into account an international driving cycle and the external environment variables at play, an electric vehicle is put through realistic load circumstances. The EV responds well to the various control strategies that have been applied to it, according to the simulation findings, which are adequate. Also the use of evolutionary techniques has contributed significantly in minimizing torque and speed ripples during the tuning process. The obtained results using GA-DTC control approach have shown their superiority when compared to classical DTC and fuzzy logic based direct torque control as it will be seen throughout this paper.

articleTitle: Mechanism for Disease Classification in Predicting Thyroid Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Thyroid disease is now rapidly increasing in prevalence among people, and it affects more womenthan men. The thyroid gland, also referred to as the butterfly gland because of its form. It produces the hormones triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4), which act as chemical “messengers,” travelling via the circulation to all the cells and tissues in the body and maintaining the rate at which our body works, commonly known as “metabolism”. Some people experience improper thyroid gland function. Hypothyroidism is a condition in which the thyroid gland produces insufficient thyroid hormone. Others may suffer from hyperthyroidism, which is characterized by an overactive thyroid gland and excessively high thyroid hormone levels. This results in several symptoms, such as a pounding heart, weight loss, diarrhea, thirst, shaking and sweating, feeling overheated, and so forth. The paper focuses on the major state of the art contribution in the field and the recent techniques available to solve this, including machine learning and deep learning methods.

articleTitle: Time Series Forecasting and Prediction of Walmart Data using Hybrid Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Time series forecasting gained attention being a popular technique widely used in different industries of finance, production, business, supply chain management, production, and inventory planning. When making predictions about a particular problem, it often involves analyzing data that varies over time, and this requires time series forecasting. Different machine learning techniques such as neural networks, support vector machines(SVM), random forests, and regression are used for making predictions. Essentially, forecasting involves building models using past data, and then using these models to make predictions about what may happen in the future. In this paper we have proposed a hybrid model by combining Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Then compared performance of proposed model with existing model such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), ANN and CNN. Our simulation result shows that proposed model outperforms existing technique using parameters Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE).

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of KNN and Light GBM Algorithms for Wind Energy Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Forecasting of wind energy is an important task for the efficient and reliable integration of renewable sources into the power grid. In this paper, we explore the use of two popular machine learning algorithms, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (Light GBM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), for wind energy forecasting. We discuss the pre-processing of data, selection of hyper-parameters, training, and evaluation of models, and the use of metrics such as mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) to evaluate the performance of the models. We conclude that both KNN and Light GBM algorithms can be used for wind energy forecasting and the selection of algorithm depends on the specific requirements of the application and the size of the dataset and more accuracy obtained for light GBM algorithm.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement by Shunt Active Power Filter Employing Different Control Strategies: A Concise Review
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper describes a review of enhancing the power quality of a Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) by using different control strategies. SAPF plays a significant role in mitigating reactive power and harmonic produced by nonlinear loads. The control strategy is used for eradicating the current harmonic which is injected into the power system because of the injection of nonlinear loads such as UPS, personal computers, TVs, variable-speed drives, etc. Researchers have already developed several control methods to boost electrical power quality. Different theories of current extraction techniques like the Modified Synchronously Rotating Reference Frame (Modified- SRF) method, Fuzzy logic controller method, Instantaneous real power theory and PID/PI/PD controller method are explained in this paper.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Human Activity Recognition Using Vision Based Method
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) is a fascinating process that involves identifying and categorizing human activities based on observations of subject behavior and environmental factors. Out of the major phases of HAR, preprocessing and feature extraction, in particular, require a lot of attention because they constitute the foundation for the training phase. The current evaluation effectively examines the trends in vision-based research approaches. Many models based on the artificial intelligence are suggested for the activity recognition; however, they couldn't perform satisfactorily on real world long-term HAR due to their lacuna in the extraction of spatial and temporal data. In light of these drawbacks, we propose a hybrid methodology for the human activity recognition which integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), where CNN works for extracting the spatial characteristics and LSTM is used for the learning of the temporal information. A complete evaluation of the substantial work done in HAR domain and its vision-based techniques would help the readers.

articleTitle: Face Recognition of Live-Feed Imagery Using the Viola-Jones Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper proposes the design, execution and testing of a live facial detection and recognition system. The system is intended to detect a face from live footage as an implementation of the famous and successful Viola-Jones (VJ) algorithm and recognize the face via an implementation based on Python libraries. This implementation uses pictures of a handful of people as training data and attempts to recognize the same people when they appear in front of the web camera. Testing of this system confirmed the ability of the system to fulfil this function satisfactorily. Within a limited margin of error, this system strives to satisfy the requirements of speed and resilience. Face recognition is the primary focus of this system, which makes use of Python libraries to perform the tried-and-true VJ method of detecting faces in real-time video. Using just a tiny subset of people's faces as training data, this method attempts to recognize them again when they pose for a webcam. Testing confirmed that this functionality could be successfully carried out by the system.

articleTitle: Advanced Blockchain Applications in Cryptocurrency and Various Sectors
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Blockchain innovation has essentially progressed in later a long time, advertising implies to perform secure and open exchanges without the utilize of agents. The paper offers a intensive examination of the blockchain technology's conceivable outcomes within the cryptocurrency and other related businesses. It looks at blockchain's potential for advancement and modern employments, as well as how cryptocurrencies are made utilizing it. The think about covers the advancement of unused cryptocurrencies, which are more secure, straightforward, and straightforward to exchange than customary currencies and are developing increasingly well known. It too looks at how blockchain innovation is being utilized to change healthcare information security and supply chain administration frameworks. It considers the improvements in blockchain innovation, such as the creation of keen contracts, which can computerize resource exchanges and dispense with the require for brokers. The investigate report offers a exhaustive examination of blockchain technology's potential, illustrating its capacity to upend set up arrange and change how we do trade within the future.

articleTitle: A Mamdani Type Fuzzy Controller with Mathematical Morphology for Shunt Active Power Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Fuzzy logic-based nonlinear controllers have demonstrated superior performance compared to conventional PI-controllers across various applications. Shunt active power filters (SAPF) have become the preferred choice for harmonic compensation, thanks to their enhanced harmonic compensation capabilities facilitated by fast switching devices and reduced losses, as opposed to conventional passive filters. This study introduces a novel approach by combining a Mamdani type fuzzy controller with mathematical morphology for SAPF. The results highlight the efficacy of the proposed control strategy in efficiently compensating for harmonics in distribution systems without compromising the capacitor voltage reference tracking time. The presented controller offers improved harmonic compensation in SAPF applications, further enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of distribution systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Corona Generated Ionized Field Environment of HVDC Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: High potential transmission lines are acting key role in the power system engineering which aids to transmit the necessary power demand to end consumers from generating stations. One of the primary problems associated with this high potential transmission lines is generation of space charges due to corona phenomenon around the line conductor which causes the major power loss of the line conductor. Secondary, the transition of these space charges at the ground levels initiates electrical shocks to the any living organism under and nearer to the transmission lines. The magnitudes of these space charge are varies with the high potential levels and insists necessity to examine the safe limits of the transmission line design. Therefore, it is very important to analyze this corona generated ionized field environment of HVDC transmission lines before designing the new transmission line and already existing lines. To arrive the final safe limits of the HVDC transmission lines at extra and ultra-high potential levels, actual practical experimental findings are time consuming process and non-economical. Hence, the scale down models of the laboratory investigations aids significant support to analyze this ionized field environment of HVDC transmission lines at further enhanced potential levels. Therefore, this paper is aimed to discuss the scale down models of the laboratory experimental analysis of the HVDC transmission lines. From the experimental investigations, unhealthy space charge ionic current levels are analyzed.

articleTitle: Parkinson's Disease Prediction Using Efficient Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a severe form of neurodegeneration that primarily impacts the CNS and results in bradykinesia. Dopamine levels drastically decrease as a result of the injury to the nerve cells. Genetic and environmental influences are the key ones that are now understood. In order to choose the optimal model for early disease prediction, we have examined numerous machine learning techniques in this study. Results were acquired after running the model's training data set, which contained records of Parkinson's patients, and a comparative analysis was conducted. KNN yielded a result of 89.74%, SVM yielded a result of 87.17%, XGBoost yielded a result of 94.87%, and Random forest yielded a result of 97.43% respectively. The goal of this study is to make a significant contribution to the improvement of healthcare and the well-being of PDpatients, so that novel therapies and treatments can be developed.

articleTitle: Fracture detection from X-ray images using different Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this period, X-rays are the main instruments used to examine suspected human fractures. It takes a lot of time to manually examine X-rays, which calls for experienced radiologists or skilled orthopedic surgeons. The primary care physicians' excessive referrals contribute to the challenging diagnostic environment and the shortage of radiologists at primary/community health centre. Additionally, the lack of skilled radiologists and orthopedic surgeons in medically underdeveloped regions, such as rural India, has driven us to create an automated fracture identification model. Digital image processing is a technique of processing an image with the help of a digital computer. In computer image processing, an edge detection algorithm looks for any kind of edge modifications. In this work, edge detection is used to first identify edges, and it is discovered that canny edge detection is the best option. In second stage, HOG feature extraction method is used to extract features from X-ray images. The images are then categorise using classifiers to distinguish between bones with and without fractures. For classification, the classifiers like SVM (Support Vector Machine), KNN (K-Nearest Neighbour), and RF (Random Forest) are utilised. This study strongly suggests SVM for bone fracture detection.

articleTitle: Modification of Vigenère Cipher to Overcome Kasiski and Friedman Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Since the advent of wireless communication, the safe transmission of data from one point to another has been of prime significance and concern. As a result, many algorithms have been developed to encrypt the data being transmitted from the sender's side to avoid unauthorized access. Yet, cybercriminals tend to always find loopholes in algorithms and develop a way to bypass or crack encryption to obtain confidential data. Vigenère Cipher is among the oldest and best-known polyalphabetic ciphers, which uses polyalphabetic substitution with the help of a series of Caesar ciphers to encrypt data. Yet, attackers have found ways to crack the encryption by analyzing the frequency of letters and predicting the key. This paper introduces a new methodology to overcome frequency analysis using the transposition of plain text characters based on the value of the characters from the key being used to encrypt them. As a result, Kasiski and Friedman attacks are nullified on the encrypted text.

articleTitle: Compatibility Analysis of IoT with 5G and 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has been the talk of the town for quite some time now, and its adoption is growing rapidly. With the growth of IoT, there is a need for high-speed communication networks to support a large number of connected devices and the data they generate. The fifth-generation (5G) and sixth-generation (6G) communication networks are being developed to address this need. This research paper aims to analyze the compatibility of IoT with 5G and 6G communication networks. The paper also discusses the potential benefits and challenges of using 5G and 6G in IoT applications

articleTitle: Ensemble Methods of Machine Learning Algorithms for Early Diabetic Detection in Comparison
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Diabetes can be an issue for people of all ages. Even everyone people among the nine is diabetic positive, which can bring more complications to humans. Furthermore, people in Bangladesh are hesitant to talk about this illness and frequently need clarification. They don't care until their life is in danger. Therefore, we researched diabetes prediction through machine learning so that people can know if they are diabetes positive quickly. The main goal is to contribute to the development of an automated system for diabetic prediction which can predict early diabetes using some basic human parameters. One of the significant parts of Machine Learning is Feature Selection techniques. In this work, we intend to focus on this part of the ML paradigm. We analysed the research data and applied feature selection techniques to enhance the performance of ML algorithms. We use PCA, Chi-square test and F_classif as our feature selection technique. Then we use the LGBM Classifier, XGB Classifier, SVC, Random Forest Classifier, and Gradient Boosting Classifier and determine the accuracy to justify our selected techniques. Moreover, We applied a voting classifier and weighted average on these models. Determining the weighted average of ensemble ML methods is a new approach to diabetic prediction. The weighted average outperformed other models with an accuracy of 96.10%. However, the main goal of this research is to provide a comparison scenario of ML methods in diabetic prediction.

articleTitle: A New Three-Phase Multilevel Inverter for Electric Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Nowadays, Multilevel inverters have received a lot of interest from researchers. In this paper, a unique architecture for a 7-level inverter with just six adjustable switches is presented. The proposed topology offers multiple perks, notably in the field of embedded systems such as electric traction drives. This topology is noticed for its capacity to generate 7-level output voltage with less number of switch, it is designed from three-level nine-switch inverter. This combination offers a high level of flexibility and control. To assess the efficacy of the proposed 7-level inverter, simulations on an inductive load were performed, followed by powering a controlled PMSM electric traction actuator. The outcomes of the simulations revealed the efficiency and performance of the proposed topology. These results underscore the importance of this research, as it contributes significantly to the design of a new 7-level inverter topologies that is useful for electric traction drives and various other embedded systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of InAs Based Tunnel FET(TFET) Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this report, we propose a Silicon and Indium Arsenide sensor based on tunnel field effect transistors (TFETs) for label-free, low power biomolecule detection applications. ATFET-based biosensor has not yet undergone experimental validation, although a FET-based biosensor that incorporates a nanogap has. The idea of a TFET-based sensor is therefore presented through an analytical and simulation-based investigation. According to the results, a TFET-based biosensor is more sensitive to two different effects (biomolecule charge and dielectric constant) than a FET-based biosensor. Additionally, TFET is compatible with CMOS, has low leakage (low static power dissipation), and has a steep subthreshold slope, making it a desirable alternative architecture for CMOS-based sensor applications. Since biosensors may quickly respond to low concentrations, their sensitivity is inversely correlated with device size. Even though Although there are several advantages to FET-based biosensors its constrained subthreshold swing (SS > 60 mv/dec) and short channel effects (SCEs) limit the device's sensitivity and boost power dissipation. The focus of research is currently on TFET-based biosensors, which have low power and excellent properties due to the carrier tunneling from band to band and the abrupt subthresholds wing, to avoid these issues. biosensors, covering everything from biosensor application. It also includes an analysis of both qualitative and quantitative parameters, such asby contrasting distinct architectures and the underlying processes, sensitivity parameters and numerous factors impacting sensitivity. In the study, there is also a brief overview of several sensitivity parameters.

articleTitle: Non Invasive Blood Glucose Level Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper describes a non-invasive technique to efficiently monitor blood glucose level without puncturing the skin. About 500 million individuals worldwide and 50 million people in India suffer from this rapidly expanding condition. Through physical activity, a healthy diet and medication, all diabetes-related issues can be lowered. The present intrusive procedure is uncomfortable and unpleasant because users must prick their finger to draw blood for the daily monitoring of blood glucose concentration; as a result, it is not suggested for lifelong use. Due to the lack of glucose measurement machines and the high cost of the procedures, people who live in rural areas and are economically underprivileged do not have access to facilities for routinely checking their blood sugar levels. The 940 nm wavelength has been found to be more accurate at detecting glucose levels. Employing near-infrared spectroscopy, the light passes through the skin which interacts with the chemical constituents of the illuminated tissue to partially absorb and disperse the light. Before reaching optical detectors, light that is not absorbed will be reflected out of the tissue or transmitted through it. So this paper proposes an alternate non-invasive method which is based on the scattering property of the skin.

articleTitle: Robust Estimation of State of Charge for Electric Vehicular Application
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The primary focus of this paper is to observe the state of charge (SOC) of lithium-ion batteries that are utilized in electric vehicles. The SOC directly affects the performance and range of the vehicle, and accurate estimation of State of Charge can prevent over-discharging or overcharging, thereby improving the battery's useful life and predicting the remaining range. The project involves designing a data logger to measure current and voltage parameters and using the coulomb counting method to calculate SOC. However, due to some drawbacks of the coulomb counting method, this is the goal of the forward-feedback neural network (FNN).[1] The information-gathering process used by data-driven methodologies relies on predicting how the model will be able to leverage the battery's non-linear features.[4] Create a mathematical relationship for the SOC without the use of a physical current by using quantifiable characteristics like voltage and between the input and output data. The dataset used for training the FNN includes features like current, voltage, and capacity. The primary objective of the project is to enhance the effectiveness and dependability of battery systems in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Multiband Slotted Microstrip Patch Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this work, a multiband slotted microstrip patch antenna has been proposed and studied. FR-4 (lossy) has been chosen as a substrate material because it has a dielectric permittivity of 4.3. The proposed antenna can be utilized for several wireless applications such as Wi-Fi, Zigbee, Wi-Max, radio LAN, radars, satellite communications, etc., considering the L, S, and C frequency bands. The proposed antenna is designed and simulated in CST software. The antenna covers the frequency range of 2–10 GHz. The return loss, VSWR, 2D radiation pattern, and maximum gain vs. frequency plots are provided. The simulation results show the proposed antenna is a good fit for the aforementioned wireless applications. Moreover, this paper also studied the optimized antenna design. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithms have been applied, and the optimized results show better performance.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Voice Modelling and Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The study of nonlinear and dynamic systems, as well as the field of practical systems, both make system identification extremely important. Because the vast majority of practical systems do not have any previous information on their behaviour, mathematical modelling is essential. To address this issue of system identification, the authors in this work suggest a Deep-Extreme Learning Machine (DELM) model trained on discrete wavelet transform coefficients. A voice model is considered, similar to the Autoregressive model (AR), for identification. The goal is to create a voice model using machine learning techniques and its identification with level-3 Haar DWT coefficients of the voice signal. The results of the comparison are presented in the result section. The mean square error (MSE) is the metric that is used to assess performance. The proposed DELM model outperforms the models developed with RNN, Bi-LSTM, and LPC-RBF. The findings of this work are able to improve prediction accuracy while reducing convergence time.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning on Human Gesture Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Human Gesture control is a new age technology which allows humans to interact with computers and other devices using natural body movements. Earlier, human-computer interaction was dependent on physical peripheral input controls such as keyboards, mouse, joysticks and physical touch screens. However, Human Gesture control takes this interaction to a new level. In the present paper various uses and benefits of Gesture recognition technique using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning discussed. The field where this technology can be applied is vast like Gaming and Entertainment, Home Automation. Human and robot working together is now not a concept but it is a working model. Effective communication medium between humans and robots are important for successful human-robot collaboration, as they allow robots to support humans in heavy tasks. Gesture recognition has been a reliable interface between humans and computers for a long time. Hand gesture is very used thing in the daily life while communicating having good hand gesture represents a good communicator. Having gesture while communication also represents the importance, emphasis on various aspects. For the continuous interaction with the computer Gestures are used. The present paper aims to explore and review the new technology with respect to human gesture interpretation using Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence. The paper emphasizes on the necessity of awareness of this upcoming technology which can be understood and utilized for a smart society.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Triple Material Double Gate MOSFET for Biosensing Application
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this paper a comparative study is shown between different biomolecules as a dielectric in a Triple Material Double Gate MOSFET. It utilises a numerical TCAD device simulator to analyse the effects of biomolecules as a dielectric on the different performance parameters of TMDG MOSFETs. Due to the non-linear behaviour of the devices, linearity testing and RF performance are significant problems that are encountered in analogue and RF circuit applications. Inthis study, the investigation of various figures of merits for linearity and RF/Analog performance metrics such gm (Transconductance), fT(Cut off frequency), and 1- dB compression has been reported. The drain current sensitivity (SI) is also major key factor which has been analysed and has been presented in this paper. Theoutcome demonstrates that the Triple Material Double Gate MOSFET (TMDGMOS) is extremely competitive for creation of biosensors.

articleTitle: A compact SPI-based SRAM in 0.6um CMOS for Low-Power IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this study, the design and implementation of the CMOS technology's Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) are thoroughly described. The Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI), an industry-standard serial protocol, is used for all of the SRAM's operations (read, write, and control), allowing for its compact size and low power consumption. This SRAM is best suited for Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications that require low power consumption and slow access rates, such as IoT-based environmental sensors. A 32-byte SRAM was created for demonstration purposes using 0.6um CMOS technology, and it was successfully tested for complete functionality following manufacture.

articleTitle: An Efficient High-Gain DC-DC Converter for Solar Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper presents a new high-power DC-DC converter designed specifically for use with photovoltaic systems. The proposed converter stands out because of its innovative features, such as its reduced number of components and its single switch operation that results in efficient and cost-effective operation. This converter is frequently called the Slim Boost converter to reflect its compact size and refined design. Modifying the duty cycle allows for an increased voltage gain and a noninverted output voltage in the converter. This allows the converter to function silently and efficiently in Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) for extended periods of time, as do the few active components it contains. The converter's efficiency of up to 95% is exceptional compared to other current converters, and it is reached during CCM operation. The suggested converter has many benefits that make it a great option for use in solar systems and other forms of renewable energy generation. In this research, we explore the inner workings of the suggested converter, explaining its component design, computing its voltage gain, and comparing and contrasting its performance with that of other converters. In addition, simulation results verify the suggested converter's operation by comparing it to the performance of other, more well-known converters.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Dark Images in Presence of Optical Sources Using Iterative Homomorphic Filter (IHF)
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Most of the conventional enhancement schemes although produce better enhancement performances in case of dark images, they mostly fail to enhance the images in existence of optical sources. The regions with high intensity are excessively amplified and saturated, resulting in the loss of original information. So, there is a requirement to effectively regulate the illumination and reflectance component for proper enhancement of an image under challenging illumination conditions. In order to achieve effective enhancement under such conditions, an “Iterative Homomorphic Filter” is proposed which is made adaptive depending on the image types. The proposed filter attenuates the illumination component and enhances the reflectance component iteratively depending upon the overall average instantly of an image. The homomorphic filter outputs after 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and pth iteration along with the original image are fused together to provide the enhanced output image which contains more information than the original. The experimental results display that the proposed technique shows improved enhancement efficiency for such images than most of the existing algorithms available in the literature in terms of subjective and objective measures.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Strain Channel High-K Gate Stack Gate Underlap Cylindrical GAA FET
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this work, a Strained channel High-K Gate Stack Cylindrical Gate All Around FET (SC-HK-GS-CGAA FET) with gate underlap has been proposed and analyzed to provide greater switching speed with a smaller subthreshold swing. It has been accomplished by improving on-current using high-K gate stacks, which increase fringing field capacitance, resulting in increased carrier concentration and strained technology on channel, boosting carrier flow by quasi-ballistic transport, and confinement of carrier. Furthermore, the suggested device's off-current is reduced by using gate-source/drain underlap. The ultra-thin strain is made up of a cylinder-shaped outer s-Si layer that surrounds the central s-SiGe layer and forms a quantum well between them. This improves the Ion/Ioff ratio and achieves better subthreshold swing for SCEs while also increasing current density and decreasing leakage current. The results show that the 8nm high-k gate stack strained channel CGAA FET amazed 251<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> enhancement of Ion/Ioff ratio over the 22nm High-K CGAA FET and 74.61% reduction of leakage current over the 22nm High-K CGAA FET. All these improvements warrant HK-GS-SC-CGAA FET as best suited device for high-speed switching device in digital application.

articleTitle: Open Switch Fault Diagnosis of Three-Phase Battery-Fed Capacitor Clamped Inverter using Machine-Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In high-voltage and high-power applications, multilevel inverters (MLI) have gained immense popularity in recent times owing to their exceptional performance. The reliability of power electronics equipment is crucial and detecting and locating faults promptly is essential to ensure stable operation of multilevel inverter systems. This paper aims to develop a fault diagnosis technique for detecting open switch faults in three-phase Battery-Fed capacitor clamped multilevel inverters (CCMLI) using machine-learning algorithms. The proposed fault diagnosis technique involves extracting features using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) technique, from the inverter current and voltage signals and using them to train a machine-learning algorithm to classify the faults. In this paper, K- nearest neighbour (K-NN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are used to classify the switch fault and do the comparative analysis. Simulations of the proposed technique are conducted in Matlab under various fault scenarios in order to evaluate its performance. According to the results of the study, the SVM technique can detect open switches with high accuracy and a rapid response time in multilevel inverters.

articleTitle: Adaptive Wavelet Transform Based Protein Coding Region Prediction in DNA sequence
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Protein coding region prediction in a DNA sequence is a challenging issue for the present researchers. An application of Wavelet Transform (WT) in Genomic signal processing (GSP) for this issue is proposed in this work. After reviewing the WT techniques applied for this purpose, an adaptive Gabor wavelet-transform (AGWT) technique has been proposed which exploits a multiscale approach to address this issue. Adaptive tuning of scale parameter plays the principal role in accurate prediction of exon positions. The significance of this work is that detailed sub-regions of each exon region of a gene set is isolated as compared to other existing methods that just detect the locations of the whole exons instead of paying attention to each sub region of them. This is important for better information regarding the diseased gene pool.

articleTitle: Digit-Size Selection for FPGA Implementation of Generic Digit-Serial Multiplication Over GF(2m)
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Multiplications over the Galois field GF <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2^{m})$</tex> are widely used for the realization of point operations in the elliptic curve cryptosystem (ECC). Implementation of these multipliers for resource-constrained applications possesses a significant research challenge. Efficient implementation of field multiplication is therefore an important area of research. We present here the design of generic digit-serial multipliers for GF <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2^{m})$</tex> and coded those using VHDL for different values of field order and different digit-sizes. We have synthesized the design using Xilinx ISE Design Suite version 14.4 and estimated the FPGA resource consumption such as the number of slice LUTs and slice registers, as well as, the minimum clock period required for different digit sizes for three different values of field order, such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m=64,193$</tex>, and 239. Besides, we have estimated the minimum computational delay and slice-delay product for different digitsizes and different field orders in order to determine the digit size to be used for the minimum usage of LUT slices, the minimum delay, and the minimum slice-delay product. Interestingly, we find that for the digit-size, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w=16$</tex> the computational delay is the lowest for different field orders. It is observed that the number of slices and slice-delay product are minimum in the case of bitserial architectures for different values of the field order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>.

articleTitle: KALMAN FILTER APPLIED TO A DIFFERENTIAL ROBOT
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This document presents the localization problem and the trajectory that a robot must follow. It focuses on applying the Kalman filter to achieve localization and trajectory estimation in an autonomous mobile differential robot. The experimental data was obtained through tests conducted by using two incremental encoders that are part of the instrumentation of the differential robot. Data transmission is carried out from a PC, where control is performed using Matlab/Simulink software. The results are presented in graphs showing the robot's trajectory using PI control and the Kalman filter estimator in a real scenario.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study to Operate Underwater Vehicle Using Li-Fi: Advantages and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this study, we investigated the viability of controlling underwater vehicles with Li-Fi technology. For managing underwater vehicles, the characteristic of light-based communication systems makes them a possible substitute for conventional radio-frequency communication techniques. The study intends to show that Li-Fi technology establishes a trustworthy communication system, which can help to drive underwater vehicles in real time. To test the communication system's dependability, speed, and range, different test were carried out in a controlled underwater environment. To pinpoint any technological shortcomings and identify potential future applications, we assessed the experimental outcomes.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of Dynamic Calcium Oscillations by Multiple Release Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The calcium oscillations in the cytosol [Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+] and the mitochondria [Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+]mit are studied theoretically via a mathematical modeling base approach. The Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ induced Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ release (CICR) process by opening the inositol-trisphosphate receptors (IP3R) is considered. The main pool of calcium is the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is focused. The simple kinetic mechanisms for mitochondrial Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ uptake and Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ release are used. However, a model is constructed that predicts the [Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+] and [Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+] mit oscillations. The dynamic characteristics of the mathematical model are examined using bifurcation analysis.

articleTitle: ECG Heartbeat Signal Classification and Detection of Cardiac Abnormalities using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are evolved as the general chronic diseases that create major threats to the health of human beings. The ECG machine can be used to track the phenomena of repetitive heart relaxations and contractions by placing the electrodes on the skin of the patient. Generally, ECG signals comprise of various types of waves, such as T wave, P wave, and QRS complex wave. The symptoms related to any cardiac disease can be traced from the morphological and statistical characteristics of these ECG waves. In recent years, deep learning (DL) has been used for medical diagnosis successfully and it helps to detect the abnormality in functioning of heart automatically with the help of ECG signals. In this paper we try to implement a combination of various deep learning techniques and pre-processing techniques for categorical classification of ECG Signals and cardiac abnormalities. As many of the previous works focus on deep learning methods, we will try to incorporate a few pre- processing methodologies to the datasets extracted to get different perspective.

articleTitle: Impact of Emotional Intelligence Training on Performance Management Systems Upshoting Organizational Effectiveness Using Fuzzy Logic Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This abstract explores the impact of emotional intelligence (EI) training in performance management systems on organizational effectiveness using a fuzzy logic approach. Emotional intelligence is a critical factor in enhancing employee performance and overall organizational success. However, evaluating the impact of EI training on organizational effectiveness is a complex task due to the subjective and uncertain nature of emotional intelligence. Fuzzy logic provides a flexible and intuitive framework to handle this complexity. By defining fuzzy variables, linguistic terms, and membership functions, fuzzy logic allows for the integration of imprecise data and captures the nuanced relationships between emotional intelligence and organizational outcomes. Through fuzzy inference and defuzzification techniques, the impact of EI training on organizational effectiveness can be quantified and analyzed, enabling data-driven decision-making. The application of a fuzzy logic approach provides a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of EI training programs and identifies areas for improvement, leading to enhanced organizational performance and employee well-being.

articleTitle: Identification of Malignant Cells Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Breast cancer has a high impact as a leading cause of death. Doctors face problems with the quick diagnosis of malignant tumors, which would help in the prevention of cancer at an early stage. Automatic detection of malignant cells is a life-saving boon. The deep learning approach extensively manipulates the data non-linearly to obtain suitable information. In this study, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network is implemented on a tumor dataset to detect malignant and benign tumors. The deep learning approach has achieved 99.9% classification accuracy with 45 epochs and 98.8% ROC-AUC. More experiments are needed on new tumor datasets to study the performance of the one-dimensional convolutional neural network approach in identifying malignant cells.

articleTitle: Bi-Sigmoidal Function Based Adaptive Gamma Correction for Dark Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The proposed Bi-sigmoidal function-based gamma correction method addresses the challenge of enhancing dark images containing light sources. Traditional methods often suffer from over-enhancement in bright regions, leading to information loss and degraded image quality. In contrast, the novel approach employs two modified sigmoidal functions, specifically tailored for dark and bright regions, achieving simultaneous enhancement while maintaining balance. The Bisigmoidal piecewise mapping function estimates local gamma factors based on local mean intensity, ensuring effective enhancement across different intensity regions. Experimental results demonstrate the method's superiority over existing techniques in both objective and subjective measures. By considering local characteristics and employing tailored sigmoidal functions, the proposed method effectively enhances dark images, delivering visually pleasing and high-quality results without sacrificing image details in bright regions.

articleTitle: A Multipurpose Smart Canteen Management System Using VHDL
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper implements a multi-purpose smart automat for managing the canteen of an institute. The automat performs multi operations such as discount offers, employee identification and sitting allocation for a college canteen scenario. The proposed model identifies the employee of an institute and a discount of 10% is provided to the employee after a proper investigation. The model segregates the employee's department-wise, by the ID provided to the departments. The sitting arrangement is done as per the department identification. The designed model is functionally simulated by using Xilinx ISE 14.7 and Modelsim 20.1.

articleTitle: Isotropic Radiation Coverage in IoT: Water Drop-Shaped Ultra-Wideband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper presents a compact water drop shaped ultra-wideband planar antenna designed specifically for IoT applications. The antenna is optimized to achieve a wide impedance bandwidth and efficient isotropic radiation patterns. With overall dimensions of 152 mm × 152 mm, the compact size of the antenna allows for easy integration into IoT devices. Through simulations, the proposed antenna demonstrates a wide operating frequency range from 2 GHz to 14 GHz, covering the entire UWB frequency range. The antenna exhibits excellent radiation characteristics, including stable radiation patterns, satisfactory gain, and acceptable return loss, ensuring reliable and isotropic coverage in all directions. This feature makes the antenna ideal for IoT devices that require seamless wireless communication in diverse orientations.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Smart Solar Photovoltaic Uninterruptible Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This project focuses on the research, development, and implementation of a solar Photo Voltaic (PV) Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) as a backup source of energy from the commonly used hydrocarbon or coal-fired in Botswana. These are the UPS system that will serve as a power backup for a connected load. The design consists of; a solar PV panel, solar charge controller, inverter circuit, and a 2-channel relay ‘for switching between the solar and main supplies.’ For the UPS system, a solar PV panel converts solar energy to electrical energy. The solar PV panel feeds a Direct Current (DC) output that charges a 12V battery which then connects an inverted circuit where the DC is converted to Alternating Current (AC). A step-up transformer is then used to increase the voltage from 12V to 230V. A relay is programmed to automatically switch between the solar supply and the AC main supply in case of failure of one of the sources and use the stored charge from the battery to supply the load when both sources fail.

articleTitle: Fall Detection Using HOG Feature Extraction and Adaptive Boosting Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This research holds significant importance as it focuses on the development of a reliable and accurate fall detection system, addressing a critical need for the elderly and individuals with disabilities who are more vulnerable to fall-related incidents. The objective of this study is to utilize the Fall Detection Dataset from Kaggle to create an effective fall detection system using the Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) method for feature extraction from accelerometer and gyroscope measurements. To enhance accuracy, various classification algorithms, such as LogisticRegression, K-nearest neighbors (KNN), and decision tree (DT), are explored. Additionally, ensemble learning AdaBoosting along with cross-validation techniques are employed to further improve the model's performance. By overcoming the limitations of existing fall detection systems, this research aims to provide valuable insights and contribute to the development of trustworthy fall detection systems that can offer timely assistance and enhance the safety and well-being of vulnerable individuals.

articleTitle: Analytical Volume Inversion Charge density Modeling of SGCG DG MOSFET in the presence of Interfacial Traps
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new analytical volume inversion charge density model for SGCG DG MOSFET. The proposed architecture diminishes the short channel effects (SCEs) as well as interfacial trap effects. The proposed structure has a gate length of 20 nm and width 10 nm. The channel is divided into three regions, the channel density of region I is kept low i.e., 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sup>m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>and for regions II and III, the channel densities are high i.e., 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</sup>m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. The interfacial traps which are acceptor type present in the damaged region III having concentration 1.5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup>m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. The volume inversion charge density model is derived in the subthreshold regime using subthreshold current model. The findings of previously published experiments are used to validate the data from the drain current modeling and a good agreement is noticed. It has been demonstrated how different device parameters, such as channel thickness and high-k material thickness, affect the device's drain current and volume inversion charge as a function of gate voltage.

articleTitle: Intelligent Plant Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Intelligent plant monitoring system have become increasingly popular in recent years as a means of improving the efficiency and productivity of plants. These systems use a variety of sensors and technologies to monitor plant growth, soil moisture, and other environmental factors in real-time, allowing people to make informed about their plants. One of the key advantages of intelligent plant monitoring systems is their ability to provide highly accurate data on plant moisture. Sensors can be placed inside the soil to measure factors such as temperature, humidity, soil moisture, which can then be analyzed using mathematical calculations to identify patterns and trends. This data can be used to optimize and improve the overall quality of the plant.

articleTitle: Biogeography Based Optimized Hybrid Chebyshev FLANN for Fingerprint Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The process of arranging fingerprint images based on their characteristics and features is called fingerprint classification. This process of classification eases the matching process from a large database. The test fingerprint image is compared with the database with respect to the classification process. For such type of complex classification FLANN is used as the classifier where the Biogeography based optimizer (BBO) is used to optimize the different parameters of classifier. This hybrid model proves to be reliable and provides high accuracy.

articleTitle: Women Safety Precaution
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This era is widely regarded as one of the most challenging for our society, with unparalleled concerns about security in our modern civilization. The primary objective of the proposal is to empower women and enable them to combat societal parasites. Our mission is to create safer environments for women across all settings. The focus of women's narratives should no longer be solely on their experiences of harassment. The proposed system aims to reduce the incidence of sexual harassment that women face in their daily lives, while also fostering their confidence to comfortably navigate public spaces during both day and night hours. The unpredictable nature of certain times makes solo travel uncomfortable for women. Numerous programs have been developed to ensure women's safety, but many women lacking awareness have limited access and knowledge in utilizing Android smartphones. The proposed method intends to provide safety to distressed women. It does not require specialized equipment and leverages existing CCTV cameras by applying algorithms to issue warnings to women. Furthermore, an alert email will be sent to local police headquarters, and the information will be logged into the MongoDB database to monitor and assess such behaviors. This project has been designed for the convenience and well-being of all women.

articleTitle: RTL to GDSII Implementation of RADIX-4 Booth Multiplier using Opensource EDA tools
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper aims to presents a fast, low power and optimum chip area architecture for Radix-4, 8-bit booth multiplier. Skywater 130nm CMOS technology node is used to achieve the desired Circuit synthesis and post-layout simulation. RTL to GDSII workflow is implemented by utilising open-source EDA tools from the Openlane framework. The proposed circuit implementation occupies an area of 16457.830 and consumes 494uW at 66.67 MHz. In comparison to existing 8-bit multiplier implementation, the proposed multiplier architecture is 33% faster and 11% lower power consumption. It also aims to demonstrate the capability of opensource EDA environment and the further advancement in opensource ASIC IP design.

articleTitle: A Class Balancing Based Machine Learning Approach for Fraudulent Credit Card Transaction Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The increased usage of credit cards for online and offline transactions in the past several years has also attracted criminals to commit fraudulent activities too. Since the volume and number of such transactions are increasing machine learning methods find a lot of applications in the detection of such anomalies. The data sets available for such cases are also highly imbalanced which add to the difficulty in the detection of such fraudulent activities. In this paper six machine learning algorithms namely Logistic Regression (LR), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Gradient Boosting Classifier(GBC), Random Forest Classifier(RFC), Decision Tree Classifier(DTC), Extreme Gradient Boosting Classifier(XGB) have been used along with a class balancing technique called Borderline SMOTE. The combination of class balancing with machine learning enhances the performance of all classifiers with the Extreme Gradient Boosting Classifier being the best.

articleTitle: Phase Locked Loop (PLL) MPPT Based Single Stage Grid-Connected PV System
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper focuses on phase-locked loop (PLL) based MPPT control configuration for single stage grid-connected PV system. The proposed PLL based MPPT technique is working on synchronization algorithm features. The PLL is introduced to offer unity pf operation that includes synchronization between the output current of inverter and grid voltage. Also, PLL based control structure is to provide pure sinusoidal current reference. The PLL is used for the monitoring of grid voltage to achieve amplitude and frequency equal to the grid level. In this research work, incremental conductance manner is implemented for the MPPT control algorithm. The performance of the proposed control configuration is examined in MATLAB/Simulink state for a grid-attached PV system. In this work, the proposed controller scheme is implemented for a grid connected PV system of 52 kW grid capacity and 2 kW PV system which is being supplied to 50 kW load. The waveforms are presented which describe the superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Charge Pump Circuits Against Dickson CPs for PLL Application
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of different charge pump (CP) circuits. Specifically, it examines the effectiveness of various Dickson charge pump circuits, including single clock CP, Taegun Yim et al CP, and CTS with DK-CP. Additionally, it evaluates different charge pump designs such as two-stack gate-controlled with bias circuit CP, Suraj Kumar et al CP, and transmission gate cascade current mirror CP. This study measures their performance based on phase noise, power consumption, lock time, and reference spur. The simulations for this study were conducted using Cadence Virtuoso software with CMOS 90nm technology. The supply voltage for both the basic CP and DK-CP designs was set to 1V. The results show that the basic CP design consumed 0.06mW of power, while the DK-CP design consumed 5.52uW. In terms of phase noise, the basic CP design exhibited -139.9dBC/Hz, whereas the DK-CP design had a phase noise of -105.18dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: EMG Signal Decomposition Methods for Physical Actions: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Advanced approaches are needed for the detection, decomposition, and classification of EMG data obtained from muscles. This study evaluates three popular decomposition techniques, Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), and Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), in order to determine which one offers superior accuracy. This paper uses the dataset of physical actions (Handshaking, Clapping, and Hammering). First, decomposition is done using DWT, EMD, and VMD. Then six time-domain features (Standard Deviation, Mean Absolute Value, Kurtosis, Root Mean Square Value, Waveform Length, and Willison Amplitude) are extracted. In the last stage, classification accuracy is calculated using a linear discriminant (LDA) classifier for feature vectors using principal component analysis (PCA). Three decomposition techniques for EMG signals are compared using the accuracy results.

articleTitle: Asymmetrical Fault Analysis Using P2P Coordinated Control System for DFIG-STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The integration of a Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) and a Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) in a coordinated control system provides enhanced fault analysis and mitigation for asymmetrical faults in power systems. Through the Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Coordinated Control System, a distributed control approach is implemented, enabling effective communication and information exchange between the DFIG and STATCOM. This cooperative control strategy ensures efficient fault detection, isolation, and coordination between the two devices. During asymmetrical fault conditions, the P2P Coordinated Control System employs fault detection algorithms and fault location estimation techniques to perform real-time fault analysis. By sharing fault information and collaborating in decision-making processes, the DFIG and STATCOM can promptly adjust their operating characteristics to mitigate the impact of the fault.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of 6T SRAM Cell and 64×64 Memory Array at Lower Technology Nodes for Low Power Design
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: SRAM plays an important role in achieving high computational speed in digital systems. Its fast access times, low latency, random access, and high reliability make it an essential component in modern digital systems. Due to its higher speed, it is commonly used in cash memory and realtime processing. However, as the size of the cache memory increases, the on-chip area requirement also increases. This can become a significant design challenge, especially for highperformance microprocessors and ASICs that require large amounts of cache memory. Thus, to address this challenge, designers need to optimize the size of the SRAM arrays used for cache memory while maintaining performance and stability. To meet all these requirements, designers have been focusing on the sub-micron level. So, this paper is dedicated to investigating the performance and stability of 6T SRAM cells in the deep sub-micron regime. It has been observed that the SRAM cell designed for the 22nm technology node has 92.0% less power dissipation, consumes 87.7% less area, and has 88.0% less delay in comparison to the 180nm node. Whereas the static noise margin (SNM) becomes worse at lower technology nodes. In addition, the stability of the SRAM cell has also been analyzed in terms of process corner analysis. The corner analysis reveals that the SF and FF are the best corners for optimum performance of the SRAM cell. We also realized the SRAM 64X64 (4Kb) memory array on 180nm and 45nm technology nodes. The memory arrays realized on 180nm consume 37.23 mW of power during read and write operations. Whereas the array designed on a 45nm technology node consumes 8.85 mW of power in read and write cycles, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Low Noise and Micro Power Two-Stage CMOS Operational Amplifier for Cardiovascular Signal Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper intends a design of low noise and micro power two-stage CMOS operational amplifier operating in weak inversion region. The opamp achieves a DC gain of 77 dB, CMRR of 79.92 dB, gain-bandwidth product (GBP) 36 kHz and phase margin of 60.92° with slew rate 13.7 V/msec. The circuit is operating at 1.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> supply voltage under total power consumption of 0.27 µW with input-referred noise voltage of 624 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz and THD of 0.7%. The opamp is simulated using UMC 0.18 µm CMOS technology. It is well suited for analog front end cardiovascular signal acquisition for wearable/IoMTs devices.

articleTitle: Compact Metasurface-based Dual-band Antenna for OFF-Body Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper presents a metasurface-based monopole antenna (MSBMA) to cover 2.4 GHz ISM and 3.5 GHz WiMAX band for WBAN applications. The behavior is achieved by exciting the dual modes of the metasurface, which are TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode at 2.45 GHz and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> mode at higher bands, using CPW fedmonopole radiators. The modes of operations are characterized by the dispersion curves of unit cells for 2×2 metasurface. The individual unit-cell (UC) is in the conventional rectangular shape, and that is designed using the theoretical transmission-line model. Then CST Microwave studio is used to design the MSBMA. The metasurface is used for dual-band generation as well as back-radiation reduction. The back-radiation reduction improves the overall performance in free space (FS) and on body (OB). On the body, the gain performance is increased to 6.90 dBi in the lowerfrequency-band (LFB) and 5.11 dBi in the higher-frequency-band (HFB). Both in FS and OB, the antenna provides an impedance bandwidth of 310 MHz in the LFB and 420 MHz in the HFB. For safety uses of the proposed antenna, the specific absorption rate (SAR) under the 10g standard is evaluated, which shows that the presence of the metasurface improves it by 99.68 % at 2.45 GHz and by 99.26% at 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A 6–18 GHz Active Variable Attenuator With Minimized Phase Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper presents a 6–18 GHz 7-bit digitally controlled active variable attenuator with phase-invariant technique in 40-nm CMOS technology for wideband active phased-array applications. A current-steering structure is implemented in the attenuator for attenuation tuning while the phase-invariant technique is proposed to reduce phase variation between different attenuation modes. In addition, the inductive peaking technology is utilized for bandwidth extension and gain flatness. The proposed active attenuator exhibits a simulated attenuation tuning range of 15.5 dB with 0.5 dB steps, while the Root-Mean-Square (RMS) amplitude error and phase error within 6–18 GHz are better than 0.2 dB and 2.5°, respectively. The gain variation at each attenuation mode is less than 1.2 dB and the input 1 dB compression point (IP1dB) @ minimum attenuation mode is higher than -1.8 dBm at 1.2 V supply.

articleTitle: Exploring the Factors Influencing Customer Satisfaction in the Hotel Industry and Facilitating Decision-Making through an Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) Based Model
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Customer satisfaction plays a critical role in the success of the Hotel Industry (HI). Understanding the factors that influence Customer Satisfaction (CS) and utilizing them effectively for decision-making is paramount for hotel managers and stakeholders. This study aims to explore the factors that significantly impact customer satisfaction in the hotel industry and proposes a decision-making model based on the AHP. Through a review of relevant literature, this research identifies key factors such as service quality, cleanliness, amenities, and staff behavior that contribute to customer satisfaction in hotels. The study employs the AHP methodology to evaluate the relative importance of these factors and prioritize them based on their impact on customer satisfaction and provides hotel managers with a structured framework to assess and compare the significance of various factors, enabling informed decision-making. By employing this model, hotel managers can enhance their decision-making processes, improving customer satisfaction and overall business performance.

articleTitle: Development of Sign Language Translator for Disable People in Two-Ways Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: This paper will help many dumb and deaf people across the world. Most of the common people can't help out with the sign language so it raises difficulty when the disabled people need to communicate with the common people. Hence, this paper develops a prototype which translates gestures into text and speech. This prototype can also translate the hand signs and converts into communicable language like words or phrases specifically in English. So, the aim of our paper is to help the deaf and dumb people community talk to those that could notable to get sign language. A software is developed that records and tracks the motion of the hand signs which recognizes by the camera and converts it into sign language. This sign language translator has been implemented by using Python methodology. A two-way communication and Python are easy to communicate with deaf and dumb people and it has more accuracy compared to other methodologies. Hence, after running the Python code, the entered text will be automatically converted to gif or simply the hand signs which will be displayed on the screen. Text to sign conversion is easy to understand and the accuracy of this paper is 99.3%.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of JLFinFET Based Biosensor for Neutral Biomolecule Detection Under Temperature Variation from 250K to 350K
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: In this paper, the reliability of the Junctionless FinFET Biosensor has been analysed under diversified temperature conditions i.e., from 250K to 350K temperature range. Various neutral biomolecules have been studied for their label-free detection namely, Protein, Aptes, Zein, Keratin and Gelatin. A remarkable dynamic produced has been captured as the variation in different sensing parameters such as Drain Current, OFF current sensitivity, change in the ratio of ON to OFF current, sensitivity in terms of the ratio of ON to OFF current, threshold voltage and transconductance. The attributes of the studied device structure have also been evaluated by adding an oxide layer over the channel in the cavity created throughout and beneath the metal gate. The studied JLFinFET device structure has been compared with UGDMJLFinFET. The results obtained show that the studied device possesses improved OFF current sensitivity and the absence of an ambipolar effect for lower gate voltages.

articleTitle: An Approach for the Supervision and Management of Power for the Solar Photovoltaic and BESS Based DC Microgrid Integrated System
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The paper presents the supervisory monitoring of sources like solar photovoltaic cell and battery energy storage system (BESS) for the various loading conditions in the DC micro-grid integrated system. The non-synchronization of power, control of frequency etc. are the advantages of DC- micro grid over AC system. The conventional control techniques like droop control, dc bus signaling control were unable to provide the robust solution in DC micro grid integrated system. This paper proposes a supervisory control technique for a microgrid comprising a number of PVs and batteries. The dc bus voltage is used as a measure for supply-demand power balance. Depending upon the magnitude of dc bus voltage, the control is divided into levels. The proposed technique divides dc bus voltage into three levels: Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3. Under normal operating conditions, there is a communication between different terminals of the microgrid, the microgrid operates in Level 1. The dc bus operates in Level 3 in case of abnormal conditions like sudden shedding or increase in loads or faults in PVs etc. Simulations are performed in MATLAB for validating the proposed research for the estimation of the various performance parameters.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of SVM Enabled PI Current Controlled MPPT Under Critical Loading Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The production of clean and green solar PV has increased in developing countries as a result of the recent economic boom in the field of renewable energy and climate change. Maximum power from solar PV modules has become a study focus due to the low efficiency of solar PV modules. Solar PV is run using a Maximum electricity Point Tracker (MPPT) to get the most electricity out of the system. Operating SPV under conditions of partial shading and at maximum power point is still a parameter that needs to be improved. The research proposes a Fuzzy Fokker Planck solution-optimized P & O MPPT-based particle swarm optimization with improved search space. Here, four different concentrations have been used to assess the partial shading situation. Through the use of simulation studies and hardware configuration, the proposed work has been validated. Using MATLAB simulation results, it was discovered that the proposed MPPT technique gives higher and better performance in terms of MPP convergence by enhancing the proposed system's effectiveness under partial shade conditions and strengthening the system.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability improvement based on firing angle control of SVCs in wind integrated system with ANN
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: The widening gap between energy generation and demand on a global scale, coupled with the imperative to reduce emissions, has necessitated the development of largescale sustainable energy solutions. Among the various renewable energy options, Wind Power stands out as a viable source capable of generating substantial amounts of electricity. However, the unpredictable nature of wind availability and its fluctuations pose challenges for grid operators in effectively harnessing and distributing the generated wind power. This issue becomes more pronounced when transmitting wind power through local grids to distant load centers. Voltage instability at local buses emerges as a significant concern in wind-integrated power systems. To address these challenges, dynamic compensation at multiple locations has proven to be an effective solution. Various alternative approach to controlling the firing of Static Var Compensators (SVCs) connected to the network is proposed in the present work. The traditional method, which relies on a classical control approach, is computationally intensive and time-consuming. To overcome this limitation, we propose the utilization of a trained Neural Network for simultaneous control of the firing angles of all SVCs, accommodating various system conditions such as change in load and wind generation fluctuations. Porposed method has been evaluated on both a modified IEEE-30 bus system and a 28-bus Indian system.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Machine Learning Methods for Electricity Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Short-term electricity price forecasting plays an essential role in shaping the decision-making process of market participants in the electricity industry, as it enables them to make informed decisions about their energy trading activities. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in developing accurate and reliable price forecasting techniques, which can help to reduce the uncertainty associated with electricity price movements. In this study, we present a comparative analysis of various short-term electricity price forecasting techniques based on machine learning methods.
